mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals supply chain disruptions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts combined with a decrease in retail and food services sales suggests a shift in consumer spending from services to durable goods, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% in 1 month and RSAFS decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls combined with a stable unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 0.5% in 3 months and UNRATE stable within 0.2%
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in strong labor market periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail and food services sales combined with a stable or increasing GDP indicates a robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 2% in 1 month and GDPC1 stable or increasing
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
